questions.question: Administrators must be able to resize virtual machines in RG1, but nobody must be able to delete RG1 or its resources. What should you configure?

options.text: A CanNotDelete lock on RG1
options.why: Correct. CanNotDelete allows updates and blocks deletion.

options.text: A ReadOnly lock on RG1
options.why: ReadOnly blocks resizing because it is a write operation.

options.text: The Reader role for administrators on RG1
options.why: Reader cannot resize virtual machines.

options.text: An Azure Policy assignment with the Audit effect
options.why: Audit does not block deletion.

questions.explanation: CanNotDelete (Delete in the portal) permits read and update operations and blocks delete operations for all users.

questions.question: A ReadOnly lock is applied to a resource group that contains a storage account. Which operation fails?

options.text: Listing the storage account access keys
options.why: Correct. Listing keys is a POST operation and is blocked by a ReadOnly lock.

options.text: Viewing the storage account properties in the portal
options.why: Read operations are allowed.

options.text: Viewing the role assignments on the resource group
options.why: Read operations are allowed.

options.text: Viewing the activity log for the resource group
options.why: Read operations are allowed.

questions.explanation: ReadOnly locks block write and some POST operations, which can break normal management tasks.

questions.question: User1 is assigned the Contributor role on a resource group that has a CanNotDelete lock. User1 must delete a virtual machine in the resource group. What should happen first?

options.text: A user who has the Owner or User Access Administrator role removes the lock
options.why: Correct. Removing a lock requires Microsoft.Authorization/locks/delete, which Contributor lacks.

options.text: User1 removes the lock
options.why: Contributor cannot delete locks.

options.text: User1 is assigned the Reader role
options.why: Reader adds no delete permission and does not affect locks.

options.text: The resource group is moved to another subscription
options.why: Moving does not remove the requirement to delete the lock.

questions.explanation: Locks apply to everyone. Only users with lock delete permission can remove them.

questions.question: Resource group RG1 has the tag costcenter=FIN-042. A new virtual machine is created in RG1 without tags. Which tags does the virtual machine have?

options.text: No tags
options.why: Correct. Resources do not inherit tags from their resource group by default.

options.text: costcenter=FIN-042
options.why: Tags are not inherited unless a policy or another process applies them.

options.text: costcenter=FIN-042 and any subscription tags
options.why: Subscription tags are not inherited by default either.

options.text: Only tags required by the Microsoft.Compute provider
options.why: Resource providers do not add tags automatically.

questions.explanation: Use the Inherit a tag from the resource group policy (Modify) to copy tags to resources.

questions.question: You need to add the tag owner=ops to a storage account without removing its existing tags by using Azure CLI. Which command should you use?

options.text: az tag update --resource-id <id> --operation Merge --tags owner=ops
options.why: Correct. Merge adds or updates the listed tags and keeps existing tags.

options.text: az tag update --resource-id <id> --operation Replace --tags owner=ops
options.why: Replace removes tags that are not listed.

options.text: az tag update --resource-id <id> --operation Delete --tags owner=ops
options.why: Delete removes the listed tags.

options.text: az lock create --name owner --lock-type CanNotDelete
options.why: This creates a lock, not a tag.

questions.explanation: az tag update supports Merge, Replace and Delete operations.
